sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Mahamaya is an organic agrochemical registration, technical-trading and formulation-growth business, not yet an evidenced compounder. FY23–26 sales compound 33.9%, but FY24–26 cumulative operating cash is −₹52.61 cr. Incremental returns are mixed and registration economics remain unproven. BQS 5.1, GQS 5.0 after the persistent-cash cap, IAS NS. Hold — unresolved IPO expense allocation and current funding; not an allegation of misconduct or an evidenced default. At the explicitly assumed ₹180.30 secondary-index reference, the equity costs about 25.5 x current-share FY26 earnings. The attractive part is tangible output and gross-profit scaling, rather than a generic agrochemical TAM. The decisive weakness is that inventory, collection and registration spending consume capital faster than accounting profit generates cash. A satisfactorily reconciled IPO source/use schedule, usable liquidity and demonstrated registration/project cash returns would change the research status. This is a cash-intensive growth/transition thesis, not a purchase recommendation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Mahamaya Lifesciences Limited, ISIN INE0U9D01019, BSE SME 544611/MAHALIFE, listed 18 November 2025. Do not confuse it with Mahamaya Steel. Cutoff 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata; source retrieval 21 October 2026 is limited to documents describing events by cutoff. The ₹180.30 reference is an explicit analyst price assumption supported by a secondary indexed 19 October 14: 59 snapshot, not an authenticated historical quote or official close. The preserved search response differs from the live post-cutoff HTML; no 21 October price or event enters the analysis. Current shares 23,405,000, lot 1,200; market cap ₹421.99 cr. Scope consolidated Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not Ind AS; wholly owned UAE FZE has nil FY26 revenue and management-certified accounts. Five-year equity horizon 20 October 2026–20 October 2031; 15% nominal pretax hurdle; ₹5 lakh position is illustrative. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold, G4 Conditional. Medium confidence in growth and historical consolidated accounts, high in reported cash-conversion arithmetic, low in usable current funding and current investment attractiveness. Audit opinions are unmodified, but the specific cash/IPO reconciliation remains open.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 canonical factors are scored once and reused exactly. GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 4, EXEC 5, EARN 6; R NS, D 3, P NS, L NS. BQS raw/final 5.08, displayed 5.1,100% factor coverage. GQS raw 6.25, capped at 5.00 by persistent poor cash realization, displayed 5.0,100% factor coverage. IAS is NS,45% coverage; known contribution 1.870 and mathematical missing-factor bound 2.420–7.370, not a confidence interval or a rankable estimate. No governance override is imposed. Moving GOV and CAP individually ±1 changes BQS ±0.20 and ±0.12; jointly ±0.32. CAP ±1 changes raw GQS ±0.15 but the cash cap still binds. Exact Decimal weights/contributions and all factor facts/counterevidence are in the score audit.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company historically imported pesticide technical molecules, assembled registration data, obtained CIB&RC approval, then sold technicals or converted them into formulations. Its Dahej plant supplies bulk formulations, own-brand products and export formulations. Technical synthesis is a separate proposed capability, not synonymous with formulation mixing. Product categories include insecticides, fungicides, herbicides and biological/plant-nutrition products. Registration work incurs studies, trials and data costs; Indian technical/export registrations are capitalized and amortized over 20 years, while domestic formulation registration costs are expensed. FY26 traded-goods inventory ₹64.00 cr is distinct from manufacturing raw materials ₹60.55 cr, WIP ₹3.80 cr and finished goods ₹12.70 cr. Separate trading/manufacturing revenue and margins are not disclosed; a pure-manufacturer valuation would therefore overstate certainty. Most sales are domestic and supplied on purchase orders; own brands move through warehouses/dealers to farmers.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Registration expertise creates a real time/data barrier: the prospectus describes six-month to five-year approval timelines and management claims an early-mover window. That is not an exclusive patent franchise. Relationships, formulation know-how and a 310-dealer network across eight states are useful but contestable. Top 10 customers were 71.12%,83.14%,76.26% of FY23/24/25 sales and 71.35% in June 2025. Management reports diversification and export contribution rising from 2.17% FY24 to 4.70% FY25, but long-term customer/supplier commitments are absent. Raw-material imports and competition can compress spreads. Dharmaj is a closer formulations-to-technicals integration comparator, with much larger disclosed capacity and channels; Dhanuka illustrates a more established branded/collaboration model; Rallis illustrates broader crop-care and distribution capabilities. These comparisons describe mechanisms, not a synchronized peer valuation or a claim that Mahamaya deserves their multiple. No verified market-share denominator supports a leadership label.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue from operations was ₹137.0758 cr FY23, ₹161.5708 cr FY24, ₹264.1486 cr FY25 and ₹328.8730 cr FY26. Annual additions were ₹24.4950 cr, ₹102.5778 cr and ₹64.7244 cr, respectively. Preferred available window is FY23–26, exactly three intervals: 33.87% CAGR. Five/ten-year CAGR is ND, not estimated from four observations. Gross profit after purchases/direct costs increased from ₹18.6192 cr FY23 to ₹54.0339 cr FY26; FY26 margin 16.43% vs 14.14% FY25. Solid production rose 272,076 kg→536,740 kg→1,169,819 kg and liquids 42,595 L→237,646 L→1,158,447 L in FY23–25. No acquisition is disclosed; FZE contributes no FY26 sales. These corroborate organic scaling despite incomplete price/mix/trading bridges. H1 FY26 revenue ₹163.0637 cr vs ₹146.2312 cr grew 11.51%; FY26 annual growth 24.50% is the latest complete comparable period. No FY27 TTM is invented. REV starts 9 for ≥30% CAGR but is capped 8 for four-year/Medium-confidence history; no extra small-base penalty or forecast bonus.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The accessible runway is formulation debottlenecking, new registered products, dealer/export access and backward integration into technical manufacture. IPO objects allocated ₹3.7534 cr formulation equipment, ₹29.4235 cr technical plant and ₹2.5254 cr warehouse. As at March 2026 only ₹0.7591 cr of the technical allocation was used; the company extended technical completion to FY28 and formulation work to FY27 because of the late IPO receipt and engineering/lead times. Dedicated remaining project cash ₹32.7936 cr is recognized, but it is not spare working capital. Further product-registration commitments ₹10.0445 cr and growth ONWC must also be funded. The organic aggregate incremental return is 12.39% FY23–26 versus an assumed 12–16% cost-capital range, not exceptional; FY25–26 slips to 9.03%. Improved utilization of old plant explains part of profit growth, so project-specific returns remain ND. GQS raw 6.25 becomes 5.0 because repeated cash absorption is persistent, not one transitional quarter.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The promoter family retains 56.35%; fresh IPO shares dilute all pre-IPO holders while ₹6.156 cr OFS proceeds go to selling shareholders, not the company. Three director salaries total ₹2.256 cr,13.65% of FY26 PAT. Related travel charges ₹0.9026 cr and ₹4.25 cr temporary promoter lending repaid within the year are disclosed; no end-year promoter loan is assumed available. Chemlinks marketing transactions ceased 30 September 2024. The full FY26 audit reports no material fraud, bank default or auditor resignation, and clean bank-return/audit-trail/IFC conclusions. Earlier ROC errors were disclosed as corrected, not erased. Promises versus delivery are mixed: actual output scaled substantially; planned FY26 inventory 118 days became about 160 days; technical capex timetable moved to FY28 with a stated explanation. Secondary September management-change/voting notices exist but original resolutions were not retrieved; do not treat those pointers as approval evidence. The investment hold concerns the documented ₹5.92438 cr IPO bridge and funding evidence, not presumed family misconduct.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 reported PAT ₹16.5233 cr compares with CFO −₹29.5239 cr. Pre-working-capital cash ₹33.8133 cr is overwhelmed by inventory −₹40.8450 cr, receivables −₹22.2970 cr and advances −₹10.7664 cr; payables contribute ₹9.3734 cr, followed by taxes ₹4.3616 cr. Cash capex ₹16.1009 cr is an investing use, not an explanation for weak CFO; reported FCF proxy is −₹45.6248 cr before financing interest. FY24–26 cumulative CFO −₹52.6112 cr/PAT ₹34.5535 cr =−1.5226 x. FY25 has three disclosed cash-flow presentations: latest annual CFO −₹0.4273 cr, RHP+₹0.5243 cr and H1 filing comparative −₹3.3054 cr; they are retained with classification differences, never averaged. Trading-stock growth ₹37.0017 cr represents 90.6% of FY26 total inventory increase. Average receivable days 66.2 and inventory 160.2 exceed prior 53.0/121.7; closing-balance days are different measures. A ₹1.2843 cr CIRP debtor is explicitly classified as disputed/doubtful yet remains unprovided because management expects recovery; admission of claim is not payment. Twenty-year registration amortization is sensitive: a five-year-life diagnostic adds ₹1.86465 cr pretax annual amortization. IC includes all commissioned/uncommissioned assets, research advances and 2% sales cash. FY23–26Δ NOPAT ₹17.7373 cr/ΔIC ₹143.1694 cr=12.39%; decomposition is ₹19.9523 cr net noncurrent operating assets+₹119.3812 cr ONWC +₹3.8359 crrequired cash. Historical capex less D&A differs from net operating asset movement by ₹0.7330 cr due disposals/subsidy/development classification, retained as an unallocated residual rather than fabricated precision. Current reported ROCE is not the CAP basis. FY25 separately reports INR 1.9279 cr issue expenses associated with its capital-raising period; they are not assumed to be FY26 IPO prepaid costs or deducted again. FY26 cash-flow issue expenses equal the INR 8.2423 cr premium deduction. No separately verified residual prepaid-IPO balance is added to cash or net proceeds. Of the INR 0.7704 cr income-tax disputes disclosed, INR 0.6909812 cr for AY2024-25 was adjudicated in the company’s favour; the revised assessment was awaited (annual report p 130). The INR 0.60 cr customs order dated 27 March 2025 was appealed on 5 June 2025. These are not equally adverse or additional settled cash charges.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹180.30 and 23.405 million shares, market capitalization is ₹421.9922 cr; current-share EPS ₹7.0597 and P/E25.54 x differ from weighted FY26 EPS ₹8.33. P/B 3.46 x and negative reported FCF yield −10.81% are cross-checks. EV using all cash misleadingly credits earmarks; available-cash EV is ₹506.78–511.72 cr, about 15.12–15.27 x normalized EBITDA. Five-year operating cases use bear/base/bull EBIT margins 6%/9%/11%, ONWC 50%/42%/38% sales, and terminal EBITDA multiples 8/10/12 x, with disclosed annual growth paths, capex and registration costs. Every case breaches required cash including pre-entry; no ordinary or non-rescue conditional IRR or entry price is reported. Algebraic equity values remain labeled non-investable diagnostics and preserve signed cash deficits. A separate counterfactual rescue funds the entire pre-entry-to-terminal cash gap, charges 2% fees, prices new shares 30% below reference and distinguishes share expansion from holder dilution. The base needs ₹46.60 cr gross, dilutes holders 13.63% and yields only about 1.90% counterfactual annual return; it still assumes revolving facility renewal. This is not available financing. Hurdles 12/15/18%, growth×multiple, margins, working capital, reserves, rates, collection losses, customs/GST timing and nonrenewal are tested. Reverse search reports no funded crossing, not a 40% growth solution. A perpetual DCF is not claimed when project cash economics cannot be established. The baseline conservatively uses INR 1.6702 cr known cash/current accounts outside the earmark. An alternate case releases all INR 6.6054 cr outside-earmark balances: its opening reserve is covered but later modeled cash gaps persist. This is a sensitivity, not proof that the extra deposits are available or that the conservative opening deficit actually occurred. Registration commitments are assumed incremental to paid advances. Capital purchase orders of INR 2.4959 cr are assumed included within project budgets; a separate non-overlap stress adds them once.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest counterargument is that rapid accounting growth partly consumes ever more traded inventory and regulatory/data capital while customer bargaining power remains high. Imported molecules can fall in price, lowering inventory recoverability; a weaker season or lost top customer slows collections, while 90/180-day facilities still need renewal. Registration delay or obsolescence can turn 20-year capitalized assets into impairments rather than recurring cash profit. The separate rescued bear terminal value is about ₹39.61 per share, roughly 78% below the ₹180.30 reference; without demonstrated rescue, no terminal return is investable. A 10% receivable loss consumes ₹7.08 cr and a 20% write-down of trading stock costs ₹12.80 cr pretax, before consequential credit effects. Customs/GST timing and tax obligations can collide with those losses. Dedicated project cash may finish plant but does not ensure that everyday obligations or new-plant working capital can be financed. Risk of permanent capital loss is High, not a claim that bankruptcy or fraud has occurred.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A 5× equity result over five years needs 37.97% annualized investor wealth growth; 10× needs 58.49%, before execution costs and taxes. Ten-year equivalents are 17.46% and 25.89%. FY23–26 revenue CAGR 33.87% does not itself establish either per-share outcome because additional working capital, registration spending and potential dilution consume the benefit. In the modeled base rescue case, terminal equity value per share is only about ₹198, far below ₹901.50 for 5× and ₹1,803 for 10×. The bull assumes much stronger margins, growth and working-capital improvement yet remains a conditional counterfactual, not independently financed execution. Evidence for enduring cash returns and scalable, attributable registration/technical-plant economics is needed before treating multibagger optionality as more than a possibility.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track: (1) the ₹5.92438 cr IPO expense/allocation reconciliation, with a published correction or detailed schedule before removing G2 Hold; (2)₹32.7936 cr earmark deployment and remaining permitted deposits, not total bank balance; (3) renewal/unused availability of ₹84.2926 crrevolving and rotational facilities before G3 clearance; (4) positive cumulative cash conversion, with CFO/PAT >0.8 x over a meaningful cycle rather than one collection quarter; (5) inventory days below FY26 about 160, with deterioration above 180 a warning and comparison to the original 118 day plan; (6) receivable days 66 and overdue/CIRP collections, with no-provision balances needing actual receipts; (7) formulation FY27 and technical FY28 milestones, qualification, utilization and attributable NOPAT/capital; (8) registration age, approval, amortization and cash receipts, including ₹1.2531 cr over-three-year development; (9) top 10 concentration 76.26% FY25 and product/supplier reliance, with new current disclosure rather than marketing logos; (10) official BSE 20/60-session liquidity, circuits, spreads and lot status before any position decision. These are research triggers, not trading orders or a claim of live monitoring.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. BQS 5.1 is mixed business quality; GQS 5.0 is capped despite good revenue growth; IAS remains NS. G2 financial-reliability and G3 funding holds override a favorable investment classification, while neither G1 nor G3 is classified as an evidenced failure. Business/growth factor scores may be displayed descriptively, but all numerical rankings are ineligible while financial reliability is central to the G2 hold. The company does not meet compounder thresholds: BQS/GQS, moat, cash and balance-sheet quality fall short. Action category is Research priority for reconciliation and funding evidence, not eligible for a new purchase conclusion. A lower quote alone cannot fix missing current funding or unclear IPO accounting. Once those are resolved, rerun linked cash/valuation and tradability at the user’s actual position size; no ordinary entry range is supportable now. Analytical research is not personalized investment advice or an instruction to trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary-content basis: the lead-manager RHP and complete issuer FY26 annual/statutory package, cross-checked against May FY26 results and the December H1 filing. The BSE source endpoint returned 403; the full annual PDF was obtained from a public mirror and matched to the filing discovered on Screener, with financial rows corroborated by a separately retrieved issuer-results PDF. This is transparent mirror provenance, not fresh direct-exchange authentication. The issuer website migrated and older financial lists are empty, so FY21/22 audited primary rows remain ND. Clean bank statements, audit trails and IFC are explicitly preserved as counterevidence. No matching current issuer credit-rating rationale was retrieved; Mahamaya Steel/Rice ratings must not be substituted. Assumptions are 25% normalized tax,12–16% nominal cost-of-capital range,2% sales required cash, maintenance 1% sales and recurring registration 1.5% sales after disclosed near-term commitments, no ordinary new financing, and conditional rollover. Key open questions are IPO expense allocation, unrestricted FD/renewal availability, customs/GST cash timing, registration revenue/capital attribution, current customer/manufacturing/trading mix, project qualification and current BSE execution. Original sources, OCR, images and personal identifiers are excluded from analytical backups; reproduction verifies calculations and file consistency, not fresh original-source truth.

valuation.valuation_method: Linked EV/EBITDA terminal model with current PE/PB/FCF cross-checks. DCF not used: product/technical project economics and funding are not sufficiently evidenced for perpetual reinvestment assumptions. Therefore DCF terminal-value share is NA, not zero.
operating_funding_assumptions: No new borrowing or optional exercise proceeds. Existing revolving/rotational debt is held constant only as an explicit unverified rollover assumption; nonrenewal stress is separate.
Earmarked IPO funds are neither excess cash nor general liquidity. Dedicated project expenditures exhaust the earmark by FY28. No further IPO money is added.

LC purchases and customs accrual are included in ONWC and ordinary cost, not added a second time. Separate stress accelerates customs/GST timing. Capital purchase commitments presumed within project budgets, not additional; a separate non-overlap stress adds the entire INR2.4959cr capital purchase order amount in FY27. Actual overlap requires confirmation.

Registration commitments ₹10.0445cr are assumed additional to already-paid advances and cash-spent in FY27/28; advances already on balance sheet remain in invested capital and are not a second funding source. Registration capex thereafter 1.5% sales and physical maintenance 1% sales are assumptions.

Opening income-tax provision and accrued interest are settled once. Gratuity/employee liabilities remain operating balances; AS operating rents remain expenses; no NCI or finance lease claim identified.
